results.refutationAttempted: Attacked plan structure for: (1) boundary leaks—verified adapter move won't disconnect STORAGE_BACKEND reference in applyStorageNotice() due to shared global lexical scope + load-order requirement; (2) single-source-of-truth—confirmed byte-identical inclusion in two HTML files with validation; (3) const vs function distinction—verified test access patterns (frameWindow.__newTabStorage for const, frameWindow['selectStorageBackend'] for function) match actual JS semantics; (4) citation accuracy—spot-checked DD1 sanitizeImportedEvents line 1220 (version===4 whitelist correct), SETTINGS_VERSION line 18, chrome.storage.local count 41; (5) coupling—confirmed no call sites outside newtab.js and test file; (6) atomicity—single set() per restore/undo with payload union prevents half-state; (7) order dependency—Task 1 runtime witness (document.body.dataset.storageBackend) validates binding, Task 0-f hash + Task 1 first-line/last-line checks prevent staleness; (8) validation sufficiency—checked Acceptance criteria are mechanically verifiable or explicitly marked [사람]; (9) internal contradictions—none found between DD1-DD13 and Tasks; (10) environmental assumptions—const binding in classic scripts correctly understood with explicit runtime verification required.

Attacked trust boundaries for backup/restore data path. Examined: (1) deny-list approach for backup (uses exclude-by-default which DD2 justifies — new keys auto-included, prevents silent data loss vs whitelist risk). (2) Input validation — DD11 requires whitelist parsing of untrusted JSON with forbidden key checks (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) and size limits (plan specifies requirement even if size metric unspecified; Task 6 case 7 tests parse-error atomicity). (3) Storage atomicity — one `storage.set()` call prevents partial-state corruption (plan references existing pattern at newtab.js:3612). (4) Version compatibility (DD13) — rejects future `settingsVersion`, accepts past versions with migration chain on reload; implemented as guard before any storage.get(). (5) Undo slot eviction risk (DD5) — acknowledged as acceptable because file backup is the real safety, not storage slot. (6) Sensitive data in backups — no encryption per PRD (Out of scope), backup file user-controlled (acceptable). (7) File handling — predictable filename format but browser download API controls path; import via file input API (safe). (8) Prototype pollution — defended by forbidden keys check. (9) Serialization — JSON.stringify/parse safely handle special characters. (10) Incomplete validation gap — plan requires size limit (DD11) but Task 6 test cases don't explicitly test it; however `storage.set()` fails atomically if quota exceeded, so consequence is restore-fails not data-loss. (11) Existing code references validated (SETTINGS_VERSION at newtab.js:18, sanitizeImportedEvents at line 1202 as pattern for whitelist parsing, canExport at line 3822). Six review rounds (R1-R6) with 15 CRITICAL/HIGH findings all addressed; no security-specific vulnerabilities remained. Plan philosophy (DD6) is move-not-rewrite to preserve existing trusted storage adapter semantics.

findings.claim: Sequential task gating via task2.pass marker is vulnerable to forgery, creating unanchored skip predicates
findings.evidence: Plan lines 429-442, 826, 860, 877. The marker anchors Task 3-6 execution to Task 2 completion via content check (plan hash, assert_failures=0, origin). Review history (R5, line 895) confirms plan hash check was added to prevent stale markers. However, marker file is acknowledged as forgeable without a CI runner (line 441: '여전히 위조 가능하며 그 이상을 주장하지 않는다' — still forgeable, we make no further claims). Mitigation exists via secondary static checks (Task 3-6 Validate at line 472 requires function existence: grep -q 'function buildBackupEnvelope' newtab.js), which would fail if Task 1 was actually skipped. Gate is HALT but with public limitation.

findings.claim: Approval-time premise verification for harness death on http origin lacks runtime evidence
findings.evidence: Plan lines 653-682 (Validation 1-e). The premise '하네스가 http 오리진에서 죽는다' (harness dies on http origin) is checked with code evidence only: grep -q '__newTabStorage' test/positioning.smoke.js (to verify adapter not yet moved) and grep -q 'typeof chrome !== ...' newtab.js (to verify check exists). Runtime evidence is deferred to Task 0-d per line 681: '1-e 는 코드 증거다. 실행 증거는 Task 0-d 만이 만든다' (1-e is code evidence only; Task 0-d is sole source of runtime evidence). Task 0-d is listed as procedural rule without machine enforcement (line 276). If Task 0-d is not executed, the premise remains unverified at implementation time.

findings.claim: Fallback documentation pattern for unrunnable automated gates allows approval without execution
findings.evidence: Plan lines 744-754 and Acceptance line 797. Validation 4 (browser execution) is marked [사람] (human gate). Plan states: '돌지 않았다면 돌지 않았다고 적는다' (if not run, document that). Acceptance criterion says: '돌지 않았으면 그렇게 적는다' (if not run, note that). This is an intentional fallback pattern acknowledging repository lacks CI/runners. Gate can degrade from HALT to DOCUMENTED-ABSENCE without failing approval. However, this is disclosed design, not erosion.

findings.claim: Anchoring via .gitattributes rule check permits coexistence of conflicting rules
findings.evidence: Plan Validation 1-g lines 677-678: `grep -q 'sha256 text eol=lf' .gitattributes && echo 'NOTE:...'`. Check only verifies existence of the correct rule, not absence of conflicting rules (e.g., `*.sha256 text eol=crlf` in same file). While gitattributes matching is order-dependent (first pattern wins), validation doesn't enforce that the correct rule appears first or alone. Current .gitattributes (read at task start) only has `*.verify.sh text eol=lf` line 1, so no pre-existing conflict. But validation allows logical state where multiple conflicting rules coexist with grep passing.

Verified approval-time validation structure (Validation 1 checks premises with available evidence; runtime checks deferred to Task 0-d per disclosed plan). Examined .gitattributes rule enforcement (existence check correct but doesn't prevent conflicting coexisting rules). Verified anchor anchoring via plan hash in task2.pass (shasum on-the-fly at line 472 prevents stale markers, confirmed by R5 review absorption). Checked rollback paths (restoration followed by page reload restores memory-storage sync; undo slot stored atomically with restored data, preventing partial states). Verified accounting: all tasks require explicit prerequisite markers or file existence (task2.pass, moved-range.txt, storage-adapter.js non-existence). Traced one full failure path: if Task 2 is skipped but task2.pass is forged, Task 3 Validate still blocks on grep for backup function existence (line 472), providing defense in depth. Reviewed denial-list vs whitelist for backup (Task 6 case 9 tests unknown-key inclusion, preventing silent whitelist hiding). No unanchored skip predicates found—all downstream gates require concrete file/hash/function evidence, not inferred state.
